answer: Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries a horizon quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. One enclave yields one identity, which means 335 clones would need 115 physical devices plus the karst attestation each must still earn by work. The ocean check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. That is 21 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
